section_summary: This section comprises records on Japanese food administration and rationing during the Allied Occupation, centered on SCAP Economic and Scientific Section Report No. 2, 'Staple Food Distribution in Japan' (January 1947), transmitted by U.S. Political Adviser Despatch No. 966. The report details the evolution of staple food controls from pre-1939 free marketing through wartime regulations to the postwar rationing system, examining the administrative roles of the Food Management Board, agricultural cooperatives, and prefectural Foodstuffs Control Corporations (Shokuryo Eidan). It covers quota setting, collection logistics, rationing procedures, and proposed democratic reforms, illustrated by extensive organizational charts, supply-demand schedules, sample ration forms, and legislative texts including the 1939 Rice Distribution Control Law.

subfiles.from: Price Control and Rationing Division, Economic and Scientific Section, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: This comprehensive SCAP report reviews the evolution of Japan's staple food controls from pre-1939 free marketing through wartime control measures to the postwar rationing system. It details administrative mechanisms including the Food Management Board, Agricultural Cooperative Associations (Nogyo-kai), and prefectural Foodstuffs Control Corporations (Shokuryo Eidan), explaining quota allocation, farmer deliveries, transport logistics, and consumer ration distribution. The report also describes proposed Occupation reforms to democratize agricultural bodies and replace food bonds with cash payments, supported by extensive organizational charts, supply estimates, sample forms, and control legislation.
subfiles.title: Report No. 2: Staple Food Distribution in Japan
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
